task: Close untyped domain handler and state inference gaps found in a bounded C++/Java checker comparison.
observation: The first 50 sorted top-level Moss fixtures had 49 C++ acceptances and 44 Java acceptances. Java incorrectly rejected uniform untyped handler/state cases, and a bounded inference pass now makes three of those fixtures pass checking and Fast Debug with output matching C++. The refreshed check-only sample has 49 C++ acceptances and 47 Java acceptances; the two remaining disagreements use distinct inferred layouts for separate instances of one source domain, which requires per-instance specialization rather than a shared declaration type.
impact: The change improves common inferred domain typing while keeping conflicting instance types unresolved. Full domain specialization, native lowering, and broader language parity remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Infer handler parameters and state fields when main call sites establish one closed type; implement per-instance domain specialization for differing concrete layouts.
